confidential_information_scope.description: Confidential Information should be tightly defined: information marked confidential, or known by a reasonable person to be confidential given the context of disclosure. Overly broad definitions (e.g., 'any information disclosed by either party') swallow ordinary business communications and become unenforceable in practice.
red_flags: definition reads 'any information disclosed by either party'
no requirement that information be marked or identified as confidential
definition includes information already known to the receiving party

term_and_survival.description: The NDA must specify (a) the term of the agreement itself and (b) the survival period for confidentiality obligations after termination. US norm is 3-5 years post-termination for general confidential information; perpetual survival for trade secrets is standard and acceptable.
red_flags: survival period under 2 years for general confidential information
perpetual survival applied to all information rather than trade secrets only

return_or_destruction.description: Upon termination or written request, the receiving party must return or certify destruction of all Confidential Information, including copies. A carve-out for archival/backup copies subject to continued confidentiality is common.
red_flags: no carve-out for legally required record retention

mutuality.description: Mutual NDAs (both parties may be Discloser and Receiver) are standard for arms-length business discussions. One-way NDAs heavily favor the Discloser and are appropriate only when the information flow is genuinely one-directional.
red_flags: one-way NDA in a context that calls for mutuality
asymmetric remedies favoring only one party

exceptions.description: Standard carve-outs from confidential treatment: information that (a) was already known to the receiving party; (b) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party; (c) is independently developed without use of Confidential Information; (d) is disclosed pursuant to legal process. Missing exceptions make the NDA punitive.

governing_law.description: Should specify a US state. Delaware, New York, and California are common neutral choices. Avoid offshore or non-US jurisdictions for US-based parties.
red_flags: non-US governing law for US parties
governing law in counterparty's home state without negotiation
